subject: biology
title: Consumer
summary: A consumer is a living thing that cannot make its own food - it must eat other living things to get energy. Explore how herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores are all consumers.

crossReferences.label: Predator (Ecology)

compareCandidate.label: Consumer vs. producer
compareCandidate.description: A producer makes its own food from sunlight. A consumer cannot - it must eat other living things. Every food chain starts with a producer and is eaten by consumers.

plainLanguageExplanation: A consumer cannot make its own food, so it eats other living things to get energy. There are three main kinds. Herbivores eat only plants (like a rabbit). Carnivores eat other animals (like a lion). Omnivores eat both plants and animals (like a bear or a person). All consumers depend, directly or indirectly, on producers - the plants - because that is where the food energy originally comes from. Consumers sit above producers in the food chain.

keyFacts.label: Definition
keyFacts.value: A living thing that eats other living things for energy

keyFacts.label: Herbivores
keyFacts.value: Eat only plants - rabbits, deer, cows

keyFacts.label: Carnivores
keyFacts.value: Eat only other animals - lions, eagles, sharks

keyFacts.label: Omnivores
keyFacts.value: Eat both plants and animals - bears, pigs, people

keyFacts.label: Place in chain
keyFacts.value: Consumers sit above producers in every food chain

whyItMatters: Consumers are how energy moves up the food chain - they eat producers (or other consumers) to get energy. Understanding them explains the difference between herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores, and why all animals depend on plants.
didYouKnow: Humans are omnivores - your lunch might include plants (bread, fruit) and animals (milk, egg) in a single meal.
